s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of swelling and pain in the right foot/ankle with associated fevers and systemic symptoms in a patient with a history of a chronic condition and skin manifestations
salient_findings: Hardened plaque and depigmentation on the face, chest, and abdomen
Hardened nodules and masses on the upper extremities
key_facts: 31-year-old African American man
Originally from the Togolese Republic
Presented with right foot/ankle swelling and pain
Associated fevers began the morning before presenting
Medical history includes a condition diagnosed at 8 years old
Tachycardic, diaphoretic, and febrile
Hardened plaque and depigmentation on the face, chest, and abdomen
Hardened nodules and masses on the upper extremities
Right foot/ankle was fluctuant and tender to palpation
Normal renal function
Leukocytosis (WBC count: 18.7 × 10³/UL)
Elevated total creatine kinase (1947 U/L)
Normal corrected calcium (9.62 mg/dL)
Depressed phosphorus (1.7 mg/dL)
Normal lactic acid (1.7 mmol/L) and magnesium (1.9 mg/dL)
X-ray and CT scan showed soft tissue calcifications

shortlist.label: Tumoral calcinosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presents with soft tissue calcifications, which is a hallmark of tumoral calcinosis

shortlist.label: Dermatomyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has skin manifestations, including hardened plaque and depigmentation, and elevated creatine kinase levels, which are consistent with dermatomyositis

shortlist.label: Scleroderma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has hardened plaque and depigmentation on the skin, which is consistent with scleroderma

shortlist.label: Sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has systemic symptoms, including fevers and leukocytosis, and skin manifestations, which can be seen in sarcoidosis

shortlist.label: Pachydermoperiostosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has hardened nodules and masses on the upper extremities, which is consistent with pachydermoperiostosis

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of soft tissue calcifications, particularly in the context of fluctuant and tender right foot/ankle, along with systemic symptoms like fevers and leukocytosis, aligns closely with tumoral calcinosis, a condition characterized by the formation of calcified masses in soft tissues.

rejected.label: Dermatomyositis
rejected.why: While dermatomyositis can cause skin manifestations and elevated creatine kinase, the presence of soft tissue calcifications is more characteristic of tumoral calcinosis.

rejected.label: Scleroderma
rejected.why: Scleroderma can cause hardened skin and subcutaneous tissues but typically does not present with the significant soft tissue calcifications seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: Sarcoidosis can cause a wide range of symptoms, including skin lesions and systemic inflammation, but the specific finding of soft tissue calcifications is not typical for this condition.

rejected.label: Pachydermoperiostosis
rejected.why: Pachydermoperiostosis is characterized by thickening of the skin and periosteal bone formation, which does not align with the patient's primary presentation of soft tissue calcifications and systemic symptoms.
